# opencode-scheduler-win

**Scheduled AI work inside OpenCode — as a plugin.**

This is an [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugin that runs your recurring agent jobs *inside*
OpenCode itself. A scheduled run is not a detached child process with a log file: it is a
normal session in OpenCode Desktop. It shows up in the sidebar, streams its tool calls and
reply, and you can open it, read it, or continue the conversation afterwards.

> The package name still says `win` because the project started as a Windows-only
> supervisor. The plugin itself works on Windows, macOS and Linux. The Windows Task
> Scheduler backend is still shipped for jobs that must run while OpenCode is closed.

## Why a plugin instead of OS tasks

| | OS-scheduler job (old) | In-app plugin (new) |
|---|---|---|
| Run location | detached `opencode run` process | session inside OpenCode Desktop |
| Result | log file to grep | chat you can read, open and continue |
| Models / auth / MCP / agents | re-resolved by the child process | exactly the app's configuration |
| Visible activity | nothing in the UI | new `⏰` session in the sidebar |
| Setup | one Task Scheduler entry per job | install plugin once |
| Overlap protection | supervisor process | lock file shared with the app process |
| Works when OpenCode is closed | yes | no (use the legacy backend for that) |

## What you get

- **In-app scheduler.** The plugin starts a scheduler loop inside the OpenCode server. When a
  job is due it opens a session titled `⏰ <job name> · <M/D HH:MM>` and sends the job prompt
  with an optional agent/model and a "this is an unattended scheduled run" system preamble.
- **Slash commands in the Desktop command palette.** `/schedules` lists jobs and status,
  `/schedule` creates or updates a job from natural language.
- **Model tools.** `scheduler_create`, `scheduler_list`, `scheduler_get`, `scheduler_update`,
  `scheduler_delete`, `scheduler_run`, `scheduler_logs`, `scheduler_status`, so plain chat
  works: *"Schedule a job every weekday at 9am that summarizes my open PRs."*
- **Overlap + timeout guarantees.** One run per job at a time (shared lock file), optional
  `timeoutSeconds` (abort + status `timeout`, exit code `124`).
- **One-command install.** `setup` copies the plugin into `~/.config/opencode`, detects the
  Desktop build, installs the commands and prints a restart hint.

## Requirements

- OpenCode Desktop **1.14+** (tested with 1.17.11) or the OpenCode CLI/TUI 1.14+.
- Node.js 20+ only if you want to use the CLI (`setup`, `doctor`, legacy backend). The plugin
  itself runs inside OpenCode.
- No runtime npm dependencies.

## Install

```powershell
npx -y opencode-scheduler-win setup
```

If `0.2.0` is not on npm yet, install straight from the repository (same command, no publish
needed):

```powershell
npx -y github:wangyuchen5110/opencode-scheduler-win setup
```

That command:

1. copies the plugin into `~/.config/opencode/plugin/.opencode-scheduler/`,
2. writes the auto-loaded entry `~/.config/opencode/plugin/opencode-scheduler.js`,
3. installs `/schedules` and `/schedule` into `~/.config/opencode/command/`,
4. makes sure `~/.config/opencode/package.json` has `"type": "module"`,
5. detects `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\@opencode-aidesktop` (or the platform equivalent) and
   prints its bundled core version.

Then **restart OpenCode Desktop**. Run `npx -y opencode-scheduler-win doctor` if the tools do
not show up.

Prefer the npm plugin mechanism? Once published you can instead add the package to
`opencode.json`:

```jsonc
{
  "plugin": ["opencode-scheduler-win"]
}
```

Uninstall: `npx -y opencode-scheduler-win teardown` (removes only the files `setup` wrote).

## Use it

Create a job in chat:

> Schedule a daily job at 9am to summarize yesterday's commits and open PRs.

Or use the command palette:

```
/schedule daily at 9am, summarize yesterday's commits and open PRs
```

List jobs:

> /schedules

Run one immediately (it opens a session right away):

> Run my daily-report job now.

Check the log, change the schedule, disable it:

> Show me the last 40 log lines for daily-report.
> Change daily-report to run at 10am on weekdays.
> Disable daily-report.

## Slash commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/schedules` | Lists this project's jobs plus scheduler status (read-only) |
| `/schedule <request>` | Creates or updates a job from the request using the scheduler tools |

## Tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `scheduler_create` | Create a job: name, schedule (5-field cron), prompt, optional agent/model/timeout/workdir |
| `scheduler_list` | List jobs in this project (optionally all projects) with next/last run and session |
| `scheduler_get` | Details of one job |
| `scheduler_update` | Change name, schedule, prompt, agent, model, timeout or enabled |
| `scheduler_delete` | Delete a job (requires `confirm: "yes"`) |
| `scheduler_run` | Start a run now and return the new session id |
| `scheduler_logs` | Tail the job's log file |
| `scheduler_status` | Scheduler state, scope, plugin version, Desktop/CLI mode, next run |

All tools take plain strings; pass `""` for optional values you do not want to change.

## Job files

Jobs are ordinary JSON files, one per job, scoped by project directory:

```
~/.config/opencode/scheduler/scopes/<scopeId>/jobs/<slug>.json
```

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "scopeId": "my-project-1a2b3c4d",
  "slug": "daily-report",
  "name": "Daily report",
  "schedule": "0 9 * * *",
  "prompt": "Summarize yesterday's commits and open PRs.",
  "agent": "",
  "model": "",
  "timeoutSeconds": 600,
  "enabled": true,
  "workdir": "C:\\work\\my-project",
  "createdAt": "2026-11-15T13:00:00+0800",
  "updatedAt": "2026-11-15T13:00:00+0800",
  "nextRunAt": "2026-11-16T09:00:00+0800",
  "lastRunAt": "2026-11-15T09:00:04+0800",
  "lastRunStatus": "success",
  "lastSessionId": "ses_abc123"
}
```

### Cron

Standard five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week (`0` or `7` = Sunday).
`*`, `5`, `1-5`, `*/15`, `0-30/10`, `1,15` are supported, in any field combination.

```
0 9 * * *        every day at 09:00
30 8 * * 1-5     weekdays at 08:30
*/30 * * * *     every 30 minutes
0 */6 * * *      every 6 hours on the hour
0 9 1 * *        first day of the month at 09:00
```

Times use the machine's local time zone.

## Settings

Optional `~/.config/opencode/scheduler.json` (read-only, all keys optional):

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "intervalMs": 20000,
  "catchUpWindowSeconds": 120,
  "titlePrefix": "⏰"
}
```

Environment variables:

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `OPENCODE_SCHEDULER_DISABLED=1` | Tools still work, the timer stays off |
| `OPENCODE_CLIENT` | Set by OpenCode itself (`desktop`, `cli`, ...); shown by `scheduler_status` |
| `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` / `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | Where the config (and scheduler data) lives |

## How it works

1. OpenCode loads the plugin with the rest of the server. It creates a scheduler engine for
   the open project directory and starts a 20-second timer (unref'd, so CLI runs still exit).
2. Every tick it reloads this project's job files. If `nextRunAt` has passed it computes the
   next occurrence *first* and persists it, so a crash cannot fire the same run twice.
3. Before starting it takes `scheduler/scopes/<scopeId>/locks/<slug>.json` with an exclusive
   create. A live holder means "already running" and the tick is skipped; a stale pid is
   taken over. The same lock is used by the legacy supervisor, so the two backends cannot
   overlap.
4. The run creates a session through the plugin's injected OpenCode client, writes the run
   status to the job file, and sends the prompt with the job's agent/model and the scheduled
   run preamble. It records duration/status/session id in `runs/<slug>.jsonl` and appends
   human-readable lines to the log.
5. If the app was closed at the scheduled minute, a run missed by more than the catch-up
   window (120 s by default) is skipped and only logged — the next occurrence is scheduled
   normally. Desktop jobs are not backfilled hours later.

Output of a scheduled run is the session itself, not a log line. Logs still exist for
debugging: `~/.config/opencode/logs/scheduler/<scopeId>/<slug>.log`.

## Limitations

- Jobs run **while OpenCode is running**, and while their project directory has a live
  OpenCode instance. Closing the app stops in-app scheduling.
- A run that needs a permission approval waits like any other session. Use an agent with the
  permissions the job needs, or keep jobs read-only.
- No retroactive catch-up beyond the catch-up window.

## Legacy backend: run while OpenCode is closed (Windows)

The original supervisor is still included for jobs that carry an `invocation` (a command and
arguments, usually `opencode run ...`):

```powershell
opencode-scheduler-win run      <job.json>   # what Task Scheduler calls; supervised run
opencode-scheduler-win install  <job.json>   # register \OpenCode\opencode-job-<scope>-<slug>
opencode-scheduler-win uninstall <job.json>  # remove those tasks
```

`install` maps the cron onto Task Scheduler (month + weekday combinations are rejected, and
two clock times become two tasks). Runs skip when the previous one is still alive, enforce
`timeoutSeconds`, force `OPENCODE_PERMISSION.question=deny`, resolve bare commands with
`where.exe` and prepend the usual Node/npm/Scoop paths to `PATH`. See
[docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) and [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## Develop

# opencode-scheduler-win

**把定时任务做成 OpenCode 里的一个功能，而不是旁边的一个程序。**

这是一个 [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) 插件：它跑在 OpenCode 进程内部。到点执行的任务不是
一个后台子进程加一份日志，而是 OpenCode Desktop 里一个**正常的会话**——出现在侧边栏、能实时看到
工具调用和回复、点开能读、能接着聊。

> 包名里还带着 `win`，是因为项目最早是 Windows 专用的看门程序。插件本身在 Windows、macOS、
> Linux 上都能用；Windows 任务计划程序后端仍然保留，用来跑"OpenCode 关着的时候也要执行"的任务。

## 为什么做成插件，而不是系统计划任务

| | 系统计划任务（旧） | 应用内插件（新） |
|---|---|---|
| 在哪跑 | 一个分离的 `opencode run` 进程 | OpenCode Desktop 里的会话 |
| 结果 | 需要自己去翻日志文件 | 能读、能打开、能继续的对话 |
| 模型 / 登录 / MCP / agent | 子进程重新解析一遍 | 就是应用当前的配置 |
| 界面上能看到 | 什么都没有 | 侧边栏多一个 `⏰` 会话 |
| 安装 | 每个任务一条计划任务 | 插件装一次 |
| 防重叠 | 看门进程 | 与应用进程共用的锁文件 |
| OpenCode 关闭时 | 能跑 | 不能（那种任务用旧后端） |

## 你会得到什么

- **应用内调度器。** 插件在 OpenCode 服务里起一个调度循环。任务到点时创建
  `⏰ <任务名> · <月/日 时:分>` 会话，把任务提示词发进去，可带 agent / model，并附加一段
  "这是无人值守的定时运行"的系统提示。
- **Desktop 命令面板里的斜杠命令。** `/schedules` 列出任务和状态，`/schedule` 用自然语言
  新建或修改任务。
- **模型工具。** `scheduler_create`、`scheduler_list`、`scheduler_get`、`scheduler_update`、
  `scheduler_delete`、`scheduler_run`、`scheduler_logs`、`scheduler_status`，所以直接聊天就行：
  *"帮我建一个每天上午 9 点总结我 open PR 的任务。"*
- **防重叠 + 超时。** 同一个任务同一时间只跑一个（锁文件），`timeoutSeconds` 到点 abort，
  状态记为 `timeout`，退出码 `124`。
- **一条命令安装。** `setup` 把插件复制进 `~/.config/opencode`，识别 Desktop 版本，顺手装好
  命令，最后提示重启。

## 环境要求

- OpenCode Desktop **1.14+**（本机实测 1.17.11），或 OpenCode CLI/TUI 1.14+。
- 只有用 CLI（`setup`、`doctor`、旧后端）时才需要 Node.js 20+。插件本身跑在 OpenCode 里。
- 运行时零 npm 依赖。

## 安装

```powershell
npx -y opencode-scheduler-win setup
```

如果 `0.2.0` 还没发到 npm，直接从 GitHub 仓库装（同一条命令，不需要先发包）：

```powershell
npx -y github:wangyuchen5110/opencode-scheduler-win setup
```

它会：

1. 把插件复制到 `~/.config/opencode/plugin/.opencode-scheduler/`；
2. 写入会被自动加载的入口 `~/.config/opencode/plugin/opencode-scheduler.js`；
3. 把 `/schedules`、`/schedule` 写进 `~/.config/opencode/command/`；
4. 确保 `~/.config/opencode/package.json` 里有 `"type": "module"`；
5. 探测 `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\@opencode-aidesktop`（或其他平台对应位置）并打印它内置的
   core 版本。

然后**重启 OpenCode Desktop**。如果工具没出现，跑
`npx -y opencode-scheduler-win doctor`。

想走 npm 插件机制也可以，在 `opencode.json` 里加：

```jsonc
{
  "plugin": ["opencode-scheduler-win"]
}
```

卸载：`npx -y opencode-scheduler-win teardown`（只删 `setup` 写过的文件）。

## 怎么用

在聊天里直接说：

> 建一个每天上午 9 点的任务，总结昨天的提交和 open 的 PR。

或者用命令面板：

```
/schedule 每天上午 9 点，总结昨天的提交和 open 的 PR
```

列任务：

> /schedules

立刻跑一次（马上会开一个会话）：

> 现在跑一下 daily-report。

看日志、改时间、停用：

> 给我看 daily-report 最近 40 行日志。
> 把 daily-report 改成工作日 10 点。
> 先停用 daily-report。

## 斜杠命令

| 命令 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `/schedules` | 列出当前项目的任务和调度器状态（只读） |
| `/schedule <需求>` | 用调度器工具按需求新建或修改任务 |

## 工具

| 工具 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `scheduler_create` | 建任务：名称、5 段 cron、提示词，可选 agent/model/超时/workdir |
| `scheduler_list` | 列当前项目任务（可列全部项目），带下次/上次运行和会话 |
| `scheduler_get` | 单个任务详情 |
| `scheduler_update` | 改名称、时间、提示词、agent、model、超时、启用状态 |
| `scheduler_delete` | 删任务（必须传 `confirm: "yes"`） |
| `scheduler_run` | 立刻跑一次，返回新会话 id |
| `scheduler_logs` | 看任务日志尾部 |
| `scheduler_status` | 调度器状态、scope、插件版本、Desktop/CLI 模式、下次运行 |

所有工具参数都是字符串；不想改的可选值传 `""`。

## 任务文件

任务就是普通 JSON，一个任务一个文件，按项目目录分 scope：

```
~/.config/opencode/scheduler/scopes/<scopeId>/jobs/<slug>.json
```

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "scopeId": "my-project-1a2b3c4d",
  "slug": "daily-report",
  "name": "Daily report",
  "schedule": "0 9 * * *",
  "prompt": "总结昨天的提交和 open 的 PR。",
  "agent": "",
  "model": "",
  "timeoutSeconds": 600,
  "enabled": true,
  "workdir": "C:\\work\\my-project",
  "createdAt": "2026-11-15T13:00:00+0800",
  "updatedAt": "2026-11-15T13:00:00+0800",
  "nextRunAt": "2026-11-16T09:00:00+0800",
  "lastRunAt": "2026-11-15T09:00:04+0800",
  "lastRunStatus": "success",
  "lastSessionId": "ses_abc123"
}
```

### cron

标准五段：分、时、日、月、星期（`0` 或 `7` 都是周日）。支持 `*`、`5`、`1-5`、`*/15`、
`0-30/10`、`1,15`，各段可任意组合。

```
0 9 * * *        每天 09:00
30 8 * * 1-5     工作日 08:30
*/30 * * * *     每 30 分钟
0 */6 * * *      每 6 小时整点
0 9 1 * *        每月 1 日 09:00
```

时间用本机时区。

## 配置

可选的 `~/.config/opencode/scheduler.json`（只读，所有键都可省）：

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "intervalMs": 20000,
  "catchUpWindowSeconds": 120,
  "titlePrefix": "⏰"
}
```

环境变量：

| 变量 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `OPENCODE_SCHEDULER_DISABLED=1` | 工具照常可用，定时器关闭 |
| `OPENCODE_CLIENT` | OpenCode 自己设的（`desktop`、`cli` 等），`scheduler_status` 会显示 |
| `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` / `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | 配置（以及调度数据）所在位置 |

## 工作原理

1. OpenCode 加载插件时同步建好当前项目目录的调度引擎，起一个 20 秒的定时器（`unref` 过，
   所以 `opencode run` 结束能正常退出）。
2. 每次 tick 重新读本项目的任务文件。`nextRunAt` 过了就先算出并持久化**下一次**时间，再执行，
   所以进程崩溃不会把同一次跑两遍。
3. 开始前用独占创建拿 `scheduler/scopes/<scopeId>/locks/<slug>.json`。pid 还活着就跳过这次；
   pid 已死就接管。旧后端（Windows 看门程序）用同一个锁，两个后端不会撞车。
4. 运行通过插件注入的 OpenCode 客户端创建会话，把状态写回任务文件，再用任务的 agent/model
   和定时运行提示发提示词。耗时/状态/会话 id 记录到 `runs/<slug>.jsonl`，日志追加到
   `logs/scheduler/<scopeId>/<slug>.log`。
5. 如果到点时应用是关着的，错过超过补跑窗口（默认 120 秒）的任务只记一条日志、不补跑，直接排
   下一次。Desktop 任务不会几小时后再补。

定时运行的结果就是那个会话本身，不是日志。日志仍然保留，方便排查：
`~/.config/opencode/logs/scheduler/<scopeId>/<slug>.log`。

## 限制

- 任务在 **OpenCode 运行期间**执行，而且要求它的项目目录有活跃的 OpenCode 实例。关掉应用，
  应用内调度就停了。
- 需要权限审批的任务会像普通会话一样等审批。给任务配一个有相应权限的 agent，或者让任务只做
  只读的事。
- 超过补跑窗口不补跑。

## 旧后端：OpenCode 关着也能跑（Windows）

项目里仍然保留最初的看门程序，供带 `invocation`（命令 + 参数，通常是 `opencode run ...`）的
任务使用：

```powershell
opencode-scheduler-win run      <job.json>   # 计划任务调它；带防重叠和超时的运行
opencode-scheduler-win install  <job.json>   # 注册 \OpenCode\opencode-job-<scope>-<slug>
opencode-scheduler-win uninstall <job.json>  # 删掉这些计划任务
```

`install` 把 cron 映射成计划任务（月份 + 星期组合会被拒绝，两个钟点会拆成两个任务）。运行时
发现上一次还活着就跳过，`timeoutSeconds` 到点杀进程树，强制
`OPENCODE_PERMISSION.question=deny`，用 `where.exe` 解析裸命令并把常见的 Node/npm/Scoop 路径
加到 `PATH` 最前面。细节见 [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) 和 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)。

The scheduler is now an OpenCode plugin. Scheduled jobs run as real sessions inside OpenCode
Desktop (and the CLI/TUI), and `/schedules` / `/schedule` are installed as command-palette
commands. The Windows Task Scheduler supervisor is kept as an optional backend for runs while
the app is closed.

- Plugin entry `src/plugin.mjs`: loads with OpenCode, starts the in-app scheduler for the open
  project, registers eight `scheduler_*` model tools, and stops cleanly on dispose.
- In-app engine `src/engine.mjs`: 20 s unref'd tick, per-job lock shared with the legacy
  supervisor, session-per-run (`⏰ <name> · <M/D HH:MM>`), prompt with agent/model and an
  unattended-run system preamble, timeout via abort (exit code `124`), run records, logs,
  missed-run catch-up window.
- Cron engine `src/cron.mjs`: five-field parser (lists, ranges, steps, Sunday 0/7), efficient
  next-occurrence calculation, optional IANA time zone, human descriptions.
- Scoped storage `src/store.mjs`: `~/.config/opencode/scheduler/scopes/<scopeId>/{jobs,runs,locks}`,
  atomic job writes, tolerant job loading, log tailing.
- `opencode-scheduler-win setup` / `teardown` / `doctor` / `list` / `status`. `setup` copies the
  plugin into the OpenCode config directory, installs the generated plugin entry and the two
  slash commands, detects the Desktop build and its bundled core version, and keeps
  `~/.config/opencode/package.json` module-typed.
- Optional `~/.config/opencode/scheduler.json` settings (`enabled`, `intervalMs`,
  `catchUpWindowSeconds`, `titlePrefix`) and `OPENCODE_SCHEDULER_DISABLED`.
- Package: `version 0.2.0`, plugin-first `exports`, `engines.opencode >=1.14.0`, `npm run e2e`.
- Docs: rewritten README (EN + zh-CN), `docs/DESIGN.md` architecture contract,
  `docs/PROBE.md` verified OpenCode runtime behavior, `docs/E2E.md` + `scripts/e2e.mjs`

# Security

## In-app plugin (0.2.0+)

- **A job prompt is an instruction to an AI agent, not a sandboxed command.** It runs with the
  models, credentials, MCP servers and permissions of the OpenCode instance that loaded the
  plugin. Treat `prompt` in a job file the same way you treat a shell script: only create jobs
  from sources you trust, and review a job before you enable it.
- **Scheduled runs are unattended.** Nobody is watching for a confirmation. If the job (or its
  agent) can edit files, run shell commands or publish anything, it will do so without asking.
  Prefer read-only jobs, or pass an `agent` whose permissions match the risk you accept.
- **The plugin makes no network requests of its own.** Every model call goes through the
  OpenCode server and your configured provider. The only files it writes are inside
  `~/.config/opencode` (jobs, run records, logs, locks) and the files `setup` installs
  (`plugin/`, `command/`, and the copied package under `plugin/.opencode-scheduler/`).
- **`setup` writes into your OpenCode config directory** and may add `"type": "module"` to
  `~/.config/opencode/package.json`. `teardown` removes only the files it created; it never
  deletes your jobs, logs or run history — remove
  `~/.config/opencode/scheduler/` yourself if you want those gone.
- **Logs and run records contain model output and prompt previews.** They live under
  `~/.config/opencode` and are not encrypted. Do not put secrets in job prompts.
- **Lock files name a pid.** The scheduler only reads the pid to test liveness
  (`process.kill(pid, 0)`) and skips a run whose lock is held. A malicious local process could
  hold a lock to suppress runs; it cannot use the lock to execute anything.
- **Don't run a plugin copy you did not get from this repository.** The plugin is plain ESM
  loaded into the OpenCode server; a modified copy has the server's full privileges.

## Legacy Windows supervisor

`run` executes `invocation.command` from the job file with that file's arguments and working
directory. Treat a job file like a shell script. Do not run a job file you did not write.

The supervisor is not a sandbox. Timeout and overlap checks only affect the process tree it
starts. They do not limit filesystem or network access inside OpenCode.

`install` registers a per-user Task Scheduler entry that points at a local cmd file. Review
that cmd file before you leave the task enabled.

# Design: OpenCode Scheduler as an in-app plugin

Status: **implemented** in v0.2.0 and verified against OpenCode CLI 1.18.4 / Desktop 1.17.11
(2026-11-15). This file is the binding interface contract for the core, surface and e2e work;
runtime facts that were measured rather than assumed live in [PROBE.md](PROBE.md) and the
end-to-end coverage in [E2E.md](E2E.md).

## 1. What we are building

Today this repo is a Windows-only supervisor CLI: Task Scheduler starts it, it starts an
`opencode` child process, and results live in log files. That is a separate program bolted
onto the side of OpenCode.

v0.2.0 turns the project into an **OpenCode plugin**. The scheduler then lives *inside*
OpenCode (Desktop, TUI, CLI): it starts with the app, runs while the app runs, and every
scheduled run becomes a **normal session in the app UI** — a real conversation with a
title, streaming output, tool calls and a reply the user can open and continue.

The plugin is the primary product. The Windows Task Scheduler supervisor stays in the repo
as an optional "runs while OpenCode is closed" backend, documented as advanced/legacy.

### Desktop-first UX

| Surface | What the user sees |
|---|---|
| Sessions | Each run opens a session titled `⏰ <job name> · <M/D HH:MM>` in the sidebar |
| Slash commands | `/schedules` (list + status), `/schedule` (create/update from natural language) in the command palette |
| Model tools | `scheduler_create`, `scheduler_list`, `scheduler_get`, `scheduler_update`, `scheduler_delete`, `scheduler_run`, `scheduler_logs`, `scheduler_status` |
| One-step install | `npx -y opencode-scheduler-win setup` copies the plugin into `~/.config/opencode`, detects the Desktop build, prints a restart hint |
| No OS tasks | No Task Scheduler entries, no child `opencode` process, no separate log tailing needed |

Non-goals: a custom Desktop panel/tab (OpenCode has no UI plugin API today), and running
jobs while OpenCode is completely closed (the legacy backend covers that).

## 3. Data model

### 3.1 Paths

Config directory (same one OpenCode uses):

```js
configDirectory({ env = process.env, home = homedir() }) =
  env.OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR ??
  join(env.XDG_CONFIG_HOME || join(home, ".config"), "opencode")
```

Everything below is relative to that config directory:

```
scheduler/scopes/<scopeId>/jobs/<slug>.json      one job per file
scheduler/scopes/<scopeId>/runs/<slug>.jsonl     append-only run history
scheduler/scopes/<scopeId>/locks/<slug>.json     cross-process run lock
logs/scheduler/<scopeId>/<slug>.log              human-readable run log
scheduler.json                                   optional plugin settings (never written by setup)
```

`scopeIdFor(workdir)`: lowercase, forward slashes, trailing slash stripped; base name
sanitized to `[a-z0-9-]`, max 24 chars, fallback `root`; then `-` plus the first 8 hex chars
of `sha1(normalized)`. Stable across runs, distinct per directory, filesystem-safe.

### 3.2 Job file (JSON, atomic writes)

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "scopeId": "my-project-1a2b3c4d",
  "slug": "daily-report",
  "name": "Daily report",
  "schedule": "0 9 * * *",
  "prompt": "Summarize yesterday's commits and open PRs.",
  "agent": "",
  "model": "",
  "timeoutSeconds": 0,
  "enabled": true,
  "workdir": "C:\\work\\my-project",
  "createdAt": "2026-11-15T13:00:00+0800",
  "updatedAt": "2026-11-15T13:00:00+0800",
  "nextRunAt": "2026-11-16T09:00:00+0800",
  "lastRunAt": "",
  "lastRunStatus": "success",
  "lastRunError": "",
  "lastSessionId": "ses_...",
  "lastRunSource": "scheduled",
  "lastRunExitCode": 0,
  "invocation": { "command": "opencode", "args": ["run", "..."] }
}
```

Rules:
- `slug`: `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`, unique inside the scope; auto-generated from `name`
  via `slugify` when not supplied; reject duplicates on create.
- `schedule`: required, valid 5-field cron (see 4.1).
- `prompt`: required, 1..8000 chars.
- `enabled`: default `true`.
- `timeoutSeconds`: integer 0..86400, `0` = no timeout.
- `agent` / `model`: optional strings; `model` is `"provider/modelID"`; empty = OpenCode default.
- `workdir`: defaults to the instance directory; used by the legacy OS backend and shown in listings.
- `nextRunAt`: engine-maintained. Empty string when the job is disabled or the schedule is invalid.
- Timestamps: `isoLocal()` from `src/time.mjs` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss+0800`).
- `invocation`: optional, only for the legacy Windows backend; the in-app engine ignores it.
- Unknown fields are preserved on update (read-modify-write the whole object).

### 3.3 Run record (one JSON line per attempt)

```json
{"runId":"1700000000-000000001","scopeId":"...","slug":"daily-report","source":"scheduled",
 "startedAt":"...","finishedAt":"...","durationMs":1234,"status":"success","error":"",
 "sessionId":"ses_...","logPath":"...","promptPreview":"Summarize yesterday's..."}
```

`status`: `success` | `failed` | `timeout` | `skipped`. `source`: `scheduled` | `manual` | `os`.
`error` empty string when none. `promptPreview`: first 160 chars, single line.

### 3.4 Lock file

```json
{ "pid": 1234, "startedAt": "...", "runId": "..." }
```

Exclusive-create (`open` with `wx`). If the file exists: read it; if `pid` is alive
(`process.kill(pid, 0)`, `EPERM` counts as alive) the run is skipped; otherwise the stale
lock is removed and re-acquired. The lock is held by the process that owns the run (the
OpenCode server for in-app runs, the supervisor for OS runs) so the two backends cannot
overlap. Always removed in a `finally` when the process is still alive; a crashed process
leaves a stale lock that the next tick recovers.

## 4. Module contracts

Implementations are free as long as these imports, signatures and observable behaviors
hold. Tests may import internals in addition to the documented API.

### 4.1 `src/cron.mjs`

```js
export function parseCron(expr)            // -> {minutes, hours, days, months, weekdays, source}
                                           // throws Error('Invalid cron ...') on bad input
export function validateCron(expr)         // -> { ok: true } | { ok: false, error }
export function nextRun(expr, from, opts)  // -> Date (strictly after `from`, second precision)
                                           // opts.timeZone: IANA name, default = system local
export function describeCron(expr)         // -> human text, e.g. "Every day at 09:00"
```

Supported syntax: `*`, `N`, `A-B`, `*/N`, `A-B/N`, comma lists of those, Sunday `0` or `7`.
Ranges must be ascending. Field limits: minute 0-59, hour 0-23, day 1-31, month 1-12,
weekday 0-7. `nextRun` must terminate quickly (no minute-by-minute scan over months):
skip non-matching hours/days by jumping. DST: for a skipped local time, return the next
existing matching instant; for a repeated local time, return the earlier one. Document the
choice in a comment. `describeCron` never throws (fall back to the raw expression).

Tests: parsing limits, steps/lists/ranges, `nextRun` around midnight/month/year boundaries,
weekday 7 = Sunday, DST zone (e.g. `America/New_York` spring forward), `timeZone`
`Asia/Shanghai`, invalid input messages, terminated quickly for `0 0 29 2 *`.

### 4.3 `src/engine.mjs`

```js
export function createEngine(options) // -> engine (see below)
export const DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS = 20000
export const DEFAULT_CATCH_UP_WINDOW_SECONDS = 120
```

`options`:

| key | meaning |
|---|---|
| `directory` | project directory of the OpenCode instance (required) |
| `client` | OpenCode SDK client from the plugin input (required in the plugin; tests pass fakes) |
| `home`, `env` | injection for tests; defaults `homedir()`, `process.env` |
| `configDir` | override; default `configDirectory({home, env})` |
| `now` | `() => Date`, default `new Date()` |
| `intervalMs` | default `DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS` |
| `catchUpWindowSeconds` | default `DEFAULT_CATCH_UP_WINDOW_SECONDS` |
| `logger` | `{info, warn, error}` default `console`; engine never throws from the timer |
| `timeoutGraceMs` | default `5000`, wait after abort before giving up on the prompt |
| `version` | plugin version string, surfaced by `status()` |
| `settings` | optional parsed `scheduler.json` (see 5.2) |

Engine API:

```js
start()                                   // start the unref'd timer + first tick; idempotent
stop()                                    // clear timer; running jobs keep their own lifetimes
status()                                  // { running, scopeId, directory, configDir, pluginVersion,
                                          //   intervalMs, clientMode, jobCount, nextRunAt, activeRuns }
listJobs({ allScopes = false } = {})      // -> [{ path, job }]
getJob(slug)                              // -> job (throw Error('Unknown job: <slug>'))
createJob(input)                          // -> job; validates, assigns scopeId/slug/timestamps/nextRunAt
updateJob(slug, patch)                    // -> job; validates; recomputes nextRunAt when schedule/enabled changes
deleteJob(slug)                           // -> { removed: boolean } (also removes lock file if stale)
startRun(slug, { source = "manual" } = {})// -> Promise<{ runId, sessionId, job }> after the session exists;
                                          //    the prompt keeps running in the background
getRuns(slug, { limit = 10 } = {})        // -> run records, newest last
getLogs(slug, { lines = 40 } = {})        // -> string
tick(at = now())                          // -> Promise<void>; safe to call concurrently (guard with a flag)
dispose()                                 // alias for stop()
```

Behavior:

1. `start()`: create scope dirs, log one line, **schedule** the first tick with
   `setTimeout(() => void tick(), 0)` (deferred and unref'd), then `setInterval(tick,
   intervalMs)` (also unref'd) so `opencode run` can exit. `start()` must return immediately and
   must not await any client call: OpenCode awaits plugin init before the instance exists, so a
   client call from inside `start()` deadlocks instance creation (verified on 1.18.4,
   PROBE.md §4e/§9.1). Timer errors are caught and logged, never crash the server.
2. `tick(at)`:
   - Load jobs for `this.scopeId` (fresh from disk every tick).
   - For each enabled job: if `nextRunAt` is missing/invalid → set `nextRun(schedule, at)`
     and persist. If `nextRunAt` is in the future → skip. If due:
     - `lag = at - nextRunAt`; if `lag > catchUpWindow` → treat as missed: persist
       `nextRunAt = nextRun(schedule, at)`, append log `missed run (OpenCode was not running)`,
       do not run.
     - else persist `nextRunAt = nextRun(schedule, at)` first (so a crash cannot double-fire),
       then start the run without awaiting it.
   - A job that is currently active (same slug in `activeRuns`) is skipped.
3. `startRun(slug, {source})`:
   - Acquire the run lock; if busy, throw `Error('Job <slug> is already running (pid <pid>)')`.
   - Create the session: `client.session.create({ body: { title: runTitle(job, at) } })`,
     title = `` `${titlePrefix} ${job.name} · ${MM-DD HH:mm}` `` (prefix default `⏰` from
     settings). Handle `{ data, error }`: throw a readable error on `error`.
   - Persist `lastRunAt`, `lastRunSource`, `lastRunStatus = "running"`, `lastSessionId`,
     `updatedAt`.
   - Kick off the prompt in the background and return `{ runId, sessionId, job }` as soon
     as the session id is known.
   - Prompt call:
     ```js
     client.session.prompt({
       path: { id: sessionId },
       body: {
         parts: [{ type: "text", text: job.prompt }],
         ...(job.agent ? { agent: job.agent } : {}),
         ...(model ? { model } : {}),
         system: preamble(job, startedAt),
       },
       signal,           // AbortSignal when timeoutSeconds > 0
     })
     ```
     `model` parsed from `"provider/modelID"` (split at the first `/`, validate both sides;
     invalid → throw before creating the session when possible).
   - The OpenCode SDK **never rejects for HTTP errors**: it resolves `{ error, response }`
     (verified, PROBE.md §4c). Treat a returned `error` as a failed run, including the
     `{ name, data: { message } }`, `{ _tag, ... }` and `{ message }` shapes, and fall back to
     `try/catch` only for transport errors.
   - Background completion: on resolve → `success`; on `{ error }` or throw → `failed` with a
     short message; on timeout → `timeout` (also call `client.session.abort({ path: { id } })`,
     and set `lastRunExitCode = 124`). Persist status/error/`updatedAt`, append the run
     record and log lines (`started`, `session`, `finished status=... durationMs=...`), then
     always release the lock.
   - The engine must never reject the background promise into the timer; log instead.
4. `preamble(job, startedAt)`:
   ```
   You are running as the scheduled OpenCode job "<name>" (slug <slug>) in OpenCode.
   This run started at <isoLocal>. Nobody is watching live: do not ask the user questions,
   make reasonable assumptions, use tools as needed, and finish with a short summary.
   ```
5. `clientMode`: `process.env.OPENCODE_CLIENT || "cli"`; `status()` reports it so users can
   tell Desktop from CLI. Nothing in the engine may hard-fail when `client` is absent; the
   plugin always passes one.
6. Settings (`scheduler.json`): `{ "enabled": true, "intervalMs": 20000,
   "catchUpWindowSeconds": 120, "titlePrefix": "⏰" }`, all optional. `enabled: false` makes
   the plugin tools work but the timer passive (manual runs still possible).
7. Never run shell commands, never spawn processes. All work goes through the OpenCode client.

Tests (fake client + temp config dir + fake clock):
- due job runs once, session created with expected title, prompt body correct, status success,
  run record appended, nextRunAt advanced, lock released;
- future job does nothing; disabled job does nothing; active job skipped;
- missed beyond window is not run but nextRunAt is advanced;
- live lock skips the run; stale lock is replaced;
- prompt error → failed + error recorded; timeout → abort called + status timeout + exit code 124;
- manual run source `manual`; create/update/delete validation (bad cron, duplicate slug,
  long prompt, bad model); update schedule recalculates nextRunAt;
- corrupt job file tolerated; `status()` shape; `start()` idempotent and `stop()` clears timer.

### 4.4 `src/tools.mjs`

```js
export function createTools(engine, context) // -> { [toolId]: { description, args, execute } }
```

`context`: `{ directory, version, clientMode }`. Tool definitions must use **plain JSON
Schema objects** for `args` (no zod, no imports): each value is
`{ type: "string", description: "..." }`. OpenCode's legacy tool path then exposes them to
the model; all properties are required by that path, so optional inputs use a documented
empty-string sentinel ("" = unset) and the description says so. `execute` catches every
error and returns a readable `Error: <message>` string (never throws). Return markdown.

| tool | args (all strings) | behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `scheduler_create` | `name`, `schedule`, `prompt`, `agent`, `model`, `timeoutSeconds`, `workdir` | create job, return slug + next run |
| `scheduler_list` | `allScopes` (`""` or `"true"`) | markdown table: slug, name, cron, next, last status, session |
| `scheduler_get` | `slug` | job details incl. last run/log path |
| `scheduler_update` | `slug`, `name`, `schedule`, `prompt`, `agent`, `model`, `timeoutSeconds`, `enabled` | patch; empty = unchanged |
| `scheduler_delete` | `slug`, `confirm` (`"yes"` required) | delete; refuse without `"yes"` |
| `scheduler_run` | `slug` | start now, return session id and how to open it |
| `scheduler_logs` | `slug`, `lines` | last N log lines in a fenced block |
| `scheduler_status` | *(no args)* | engine status, version, desktop/CLI mode, next run |

Descriptions must mention the session appears in the OpenCode sidebar and that cron is
5-field. Keep descriptions under ~400 chars each.

Tests: schema shape (args are JSON-Schema objects, no zod), each tool happy path against a
fake engine, error path returns string starting with `Error:`, `scheduler_delete` refuses
without confirm, `scheduler_update` sends only non-empty fields.

### 4.5 `src/plugin.mjs`

```js
export const SchedulerPlugin = async (input, options = {}) => { ... }  // returns hooks
export default { id: "scheduler", server: SchedulerPlugin }
```

- `input` is the OpenCode plugin input: `{ directory, worktree, client, project, serverUrl, $ }`.
- Resolve settings from `<configDir>/scheduler.json` (missing/invalid → defaults; log once).
- Create one engine per instance with `{ directory: input.directory, client: input.client,
  ...settings, version }`; call `engine.start()` unless `settings.enabled === false` or
  `env.OPENCODE_SCHEDULER_DISABLED === "1"`.
- Return hooks: `tool: createTools(engine, ctx)`, `dispose: async () => engine.stop()`,
  and an `event` hook that logs `session.error` for sessions created by this engine only
  (best effort; keep it cheap and non-throwing).
- Never throw from plugin init: wrap startup in try/catch, return tools backed by an engine
  whose timer may be off, and log the failure.
- Must not import `@opencode-ai/plugin`/`zod` (zero deps): the plugin is copied into the
  user config as plain files.
- The plugin file must work as a **legacy** export (function module) too: keep
  `SchedulerPlugin` the only function export besides the default object, or make the entry
  re-export a single function (see 5.1).

## Isolation

Every run creates `%TEMP%\sched-e2e\<UTC-stamp>-<random>\` with `config/`, `data/`, `cache/`,
`state/`, `project/` and `logs/` and passes them to OpenCode as `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`,
`XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`. `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` and
`OPENCODE_SCHEDULER_DISABLED` are removed from the child environment, so the run can never pick
up the user's real OpenCode config or running Desktop instance. The temp tree is deleted on
exit unless `--keep` is passed.

The only interaction with the real user data is the **opt-in** `--with-model` copy of
`~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` into the isolated data dir. The file is copied byte-for-byte
and never read into a log or displayed.

## What the run does

1. **Install** — `node bin/opencode-scheduler-win.mjs setup --config-dir <isolated>`; checks the
   generated `plugin/opencode-scheduler.js` entry, the copied `.opencode-scheduler/src/*.mjs`
   sources, `command/schedules.md` and `command/schedule.md`.
2. **Start** — `opencode serve --port <free> --hostname 127.0.0.1 --print-logs --log-level WARN`
   with `cwd` = temp project and `OPENCODE_CLIENT=desktop`; stdout/stderr go to a log **file
   descriptor** (this sandbox denies piped stdio). The port is picked with `net.listen(0)` —
   `--port 0` is not random on 1.18.4 (it resolves to 4096), see `docs/PROBE.md`.
3. **Ready** — `GET /app` must answer 200 (budget 30 s).
4. **Plugin loaded** — poll `GET /experimental/tool/ids` until all eight `scheduler_*` ids appear
   (budget 30 s). This request is what creates the directory instance and runs plugin init, so a
   deadlocked init fails here instead of hanging the run.
5. **Schemas** — `GET /experimental/tool?provider=&model=`: every tool has a plain JSON-Schema
   `parameters` object with `type: "string"` properties, every declared property is listed in
   `required`, and `scheduler_status` declares no arguments.
6. **Commands** — `GET /command` lists `schedules` and `schedule` with `source: "command"` and a
   non-empty template.
7. **Discovery** — `GET /config` lists the installed entry.
8. **Log** — the server log contains no `failed to load plugin` (a runtime init throw is logged
   there; note that syntax errors are silent, which is why the tool assertion is the real gate).
9. **Scheduled run** — a due job is planted in
   `<cfg>/scheduler/scopes/<scopeId>/jobs/e2e.json` (`schedule: "* * * * *"`,
   `nextRunAt` 5 s in the past, `enabled: true`) **before** the server starts, so the engine's
   first tick sees it. Then the script polls `GET /session?directory=<project>` for a title
   starting with `⏰` and the job file for a settled `lastRunStatus` (budget 90 s), and checks:
   session title prefix, `lastSessionId` wiring, run record in `runs/e2e.jsonl`, job log file,
   run-record status matches the job, and (on success) an assistant message stored for the
   session.
10. **Shutdown** — `POST /instance/dispose` must be accepted, then `child.kill()` must stop the
    server and free the port (budget 15 s). A `taskkill /T /F` tree kill is attempted only as a
    Windows fallback and its denial is not treated as a failure.

Failure logging includes the last `GET /session` body, the job file JSON, the resolved
`/config/providers` default models and the server log tail, so a failure is diagnosable without
re-running.

## Environment limitations (documented, with evidence)

These are properties of the machine/sandbox, not of the plugin:

1. **Piped stdio is denied** in the agent sandbox (`spawn EPERM`). The script always spawns with
   `stdio: ["ignore", logFd, logFd]`. This is also why the e2e cannot be "run under a debugger";
   inspect the log path printed at startup instead (`--keep` keeps it).
2. **`taskkill /T /F` is denied** in this sandbox (`ERROR: Access denied`). `child.kill()` is the
   primary and measured shutdown path (SIGTERM, 10–135 ms, port freed). The `taskkill` call stays
   as a best-effort fallback for normal shells.
3. **`--with-model` without `--model` can fail on the default model.** With the user's real
   `auth.json`, this machine's provider defaults resolve to
   `{"google":"gemini-3-pro-image","deepseek":"deepseek-v4-pro",…}` and OpenCode picks
   `google/gemini-3-pro-image`, whose free-tier quota is exhausted. The provider call retries and
   never settles, so the run stays `running` past the 90 s budget and the script fails with
   `status=running (no --model given: the server default model may be quota-limited; pass
   --model provider/modelID)`, printing the defaults and the server log tail as evidence.
   Pinning a model fixes it: `--with-model --model deepseek/deepseek-flash` →
   **27/27 PASS, real assistant reply, scheduled run 3.1 s**. Also verified working in the same
   setup: `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` (~1.5 s) and `moonshotai-cn/kimi-k3` (~13 s);
   `minimax-coding-plan/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` fails provider auth (`X-Api-Key` header).
4. **Network is required for the default run.** Without a copied `auth.json`, the isolated data
   dir still has OpenCode Zen's public provider (`opencode`, model `big-pickle`) and the scheduled
   prompt succeeds in ~5.5 s. If the machine is offline the run status becomes `failed`; the
   script accepts a non-`success` settled status when `--with-model` is **not** used (all
   structural assertions still must pass) and reports the outcome instead of hiding it.
5. **A benign warning is expected in the log**: `background dependency install failed …
   @opencode-ai/plugin … EPERM`. Plugins load from plain files regardless; the script reports it
   as `INFO`, not as a failure.
6. `GET /tool` does not exist on 1.18.4 (returns the web-UI HTML). The script uses
   `GET /experimental/tool/ids` and `GET /experimental/tool?provider=&model=`; see
   `docs/PROBE.md` for the exact payloads.

## Debugging a failure

* Re-run with `--keep --verbose`, then open the printed temp root:
  `logs/setup.log`, `logs/serve.log`, `config/opencode/scheduler/scopes/*/jobs/e2e.json`,
  `config/opencode/scheduler/scopes/*/runs/e2e.jsonl`,
  `config/opencode/logs/scheduler/*/e2e.log`.
* If `all 8 scheduler_* tools registered` fails, the plugin did not load. Check
  `logs/serve.log` for `failed to load plugin` (runtime error) — a syntax error or a missing
  relative import is silent, so also check that
  `config/opencode/plugin/.opencode-scheduler/src/` contains every `src/*.mjs` file.
* If the session appears but the status never settles, the provider hangs (see limitation 3) or
  `timeoutSeconds`/abort handling regressed.
* Run `node scripts/e2e.mjs` a second time to rule out transient startup/network slowness.

Check server logs for details.",ref:"err_c1a57a24"}},response:{status:500}}` — data undefined | | prompt with unknown modelID on a real provider | same 500 `UnknownError` | | `session.create({body:{title:12345}})` | `{error:{_tag:"BadRequest"},response:{status:400}}` (no message field!) | | `session.get` / `prompt` on unknown session | `{error:{name:"NotFoundError",data:{message:"Session not found: ses_…"}},response:{status:404}}` | | `session.abort` on unknown session | `{data:true}`, status 200 — **no error** | So DESIGN §4.3 “handle `{data,error}`: throw a readable error on `error`” is **required**; a bare try/catch around `await client.session.prompt(...)` would mark failed runs as `success`. JSON.stringify(env.error)`. ### 4d. “No provider/model configured” There is no provider-less state in an isolated 1.18.4 install: `GET /config/providers` reports provider `opencode` (“OpenCode Zen”, `apiKey: "public"`) and `default: {"opencode":"big-pickle"}`. An isolated run with no copied `auth.json` therefore **succeeds** at prompting: ``` stream providerID=opencode modelID=big-pickle … "Hello" ``` Relevant to e2e: a scheduled run against an isolated data dir will genuinely complete (it needs network). To test the failure path, pass an unknown model instead — that is the 500 envelope above, and the server stays healthy (`GET /session`, `GET /global/health` still 200) — no crash. ### 4e. ⚠️ Deadlock: do NOT await a client call inside plugin init `probe13b.mjs` result: | first action in plugin init | outcome | |---|---| | `await input.client.session.create(...)` **inside init** | **DEADLOCK**. The scoped request that triggers instance creation never returns (15 s timeout), instance never finishes bootstrapping (no `message=init` log), server keeps listening but that directory is unusable forever. | | same call in `setTimeout(..., 0)` after init returns | works (instance ready in ~1.4 s, session created, `GET /session` OK) | | same call in `setTimeout(..., 1000)` with `.unref()` | works | Consequence for DESIGN §4.3.1 (`start(): … run tick() once, then setInterval`): the first tick must be **fire-and-forget / deferred** (`setTimeout(() => void this.tick(), 0)` or `setImmediate`), and `start()` must not be awaited by plugin init. `tick()` itself must not hold the instance-open promise. ### 4f. Hooks supported by 1.18.4 Returning `{ tool, event, dispose }` works: * `tool` — object, registered as above. * `event` — called with `{ event }`; observed types include `session.created` for sessions created through the client. Cheap and non-throwing, as DESIGN §4.5 assumes. * `dispose` — called on `POST /instance/dispose` (200 `true`), on `POST /global/dispose` (200 `true`) and on process shutdown (`opencode run` exit). After dispose, the next request for that directory creates a **new** instance and calls init again. --- ## 5. `opencode serve` on Windows — exact recipe and measured timing ### Startup ```js const port = await freePort(); // pick via net.createServer listen(0) const logFd = fs.openSync(logPath, "a"); // piped stdio is denied in this sandbox const child = spawn("D:\\tools\\opencode\\opencode.exe", ["serve", "--port", String(port), "--hostname", "127.0.0.1", "--print-logs", "--log-level", "WARN"], { cwd: projectDir, env: isoEnv, stdio: ["ignore", logFd, logFd], windowsHide: true }); ``` Readiness, in order (both are needed): 1. `GET http://127.0.0.1:/app` → `200` (web-UI HTML). **Does not create the instance.** 2. `GET http://127.0.0.1:/experimental/tool/ids` → `200`. Handy for the engine only as a fallback; the injected client is bound to the right instance and should be preferred. --- ## 7. Per-directory plugin instances — VERIFIED With one `serve` process and two project directories A (server cwd) and B (a sibling temp dir): * `POST /session?directory=B` (or any scoped GET) creates a **second instance** in the same OS process (`creating instance directory=…projectB`), and the plugin `init` runs **once per directory** (2 inits, same pid, same `serverUrl`). * Both instances **stay alive concurrently**: heartbeat timers from A and B kept ticking while the other was in use. Opening B did **not** dispose A; `dispose` was only called on explicit `/instance/dispose` / `/global/dispose` / process exit. * `input.directory` equals that instance’s directory (`…\project` / `…\projectB`), while `process.cwd()` stays the server spawn cwd for both — never use `process.cwd()` in the plugin. * The injected client is instance-bound: sessions created from B’s plugin land in `projectB` (also proven by `GET /session?directory=…` grouping). * Consequently each directory gets its **own engine**, its own scope id (DESIGN `scopeIdFor(directory)`), and its own timer — matches DESIGN §3.1/§4.3. `input.worktree` was `"/"` and `project.id` `"global"` for a non-git temp dir; inside a git repo the worktree is the repo root.
